result_text:
Any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` now counts as mock resources, whatever the rest of the name is. That covers a plain `mock/`, `mock.data`, `mock(old)`, `mock-größe` and `mock模拟`. I haven't tested those cases, including backslash paths. The existing scoping and convention tests in `codeanalyzer` pass.

In `ScopingConventions.java` (lines 393–394), I replaced the two folder patterns `.*/__mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*` and `.*/mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*` with `.*/__mock[^/]*/.*` and `.*/mock[^/]*/.*`.

- **Single folder name:** the match stays within one folder name and still needs a `/` after it. Files under `remock/`, `demo/` or `src/main/java/`, and files named `mock.java` or `mockery.java`, stay out of test code.
- **Old folders:** `mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `mock-data/`, `mock_data/`, `mock data/` and `mockStore/` still match.
- **Backslash paths:** `SourceFileFilter.matches` already tries the path with `\` converted to `/`, so Windows-style paths work without further changes.

I didn't add new test cases.
